races.name: Summer Saturday Series At Doncaster Racecourse Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: The Ubermensch
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has been runner-up twice in handicaps and kept on well over shorter at Wolverhampton last time.
runners_data.comment: 0-7 but he still has potential and looks interesting at this new trip; cheekpieces added
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 but he's finished runner-up in two of his four handicaps and he kept on well when fourth at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) last month; looks worth a try at this new trip and he's in the mix with cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: It's Only Fun
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse coming off a 20-1 victory at Southwell where cheekpieces helped, now 4lb higher but suited by the likely pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Cashed in on a reduced mark when scoring at Southwell (1m3f) last month; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Took advantage of a reduced mark when battling well to score at 20-1 at Southwell (1m3f, AW; cheekpieces reapplied) two weeks ago; back up 4lb in the weights but he remains well treated on old form and his first win was on turf; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Animato
runners_data.note: Front-running veteran returning from 314-day break after hurdling campaign, will dictate pace but may struggle late against fresher opponents.
runners_data.comment: His last win was over 2m in May 2024; has work to do back on the Flat after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time Flat winner but last two were over 2m at Catterick in May 2024; well handicapped on old form but has mixed record since switched to hurdling in his last seven starts; returns after a break but his tactical speed will be tested back in this sphere and others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Sweet Kiss
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with strong record under Dickson but disappointing this season, needs to rediscover last year's form to feature prominently.
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times under Jake Dickson last August/September (1m2f, good to firm-good to soft); no impact in two runs this season but she caught the eye with her late headway at Carlisle (1m3f, good) last Friday; has claims if she can build on that and she won't mind what the weather does.

runners_data.name: Division Day
runners_data.note: Dual winner returning from four-month break having focused on hurdling, hold-up style suits but fitness could be a concern.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up over hurdles in last two starts and he needs a close look back on the Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 1m6f Flat winner who has finished runner-up in novice/maiden hurdles (2m/2m4f) in his last two runs; returns after four months off but he's only 1lb higher than for his last win and it would be a positive if the forecast rain arrives; needs a close look back on the Flat.

runners_data.name: Letmeseethecolts
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who peaked with Pontefract win last April but has struggled in two runs since then.
runners_data.comment: Easy win at Pontefract last April but she's been out of sorts in both subsequent runs
runners_data.spotlight: Hit a personal best with her clearcut win at Pontefract (1m4f, good) last April but she's had only two runs since and has struggled in both of them; has some questions to answer and she needs a major revival back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Muhib
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse with creditable spring efforts including third at Catterick, well-weighted with significant apprentice allowance.
runners_data.comment: Some good efforts this spring but he was well held last time and is now 0-23
runners_data.spotlight: Some creditable efforts this spring including when third at Catterick (1m4f, good) last month; hard to rule out another good run but he didn't really fire at Pontefract last time and his overall record is now 0-23.

races.paceDynamic: Animato will take the field along as the sole confirmed front runner, with Letmeseethecolts potentially tracking prominently. The majority of this field comprises hold-up horses (The Ubermensch, It's Only Fun, Sweet Kiss, Division Day, Muhib), meaning Animato can dictate a comfortable tempo without pressure. At 1m4f on good to firm ground, the sustained pace will likely be moderate early before quickening from the 3f pole. This race shape clearly favours the hold-up merchants who can deliver their finishing kicks late, as Animato may struggle to resist the wave of closers over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Animato sets uncontested fractions and the pace quickens late.
scenarios.body: The patient tactics of the hold-up brigade play perfectly into their hands as they sweep past a weakening pace-setter. Multiple horses with finishing kicks converge in the final furlong with The Ubermensch and It's Only Fun best placed to capitalize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Resist
scenarios.trigger: If Animato and Letmeseethecolts work together to maintain a strong gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Their combined early speed creates enough tempo to blunt the finishing kicks of the hold-up horses. Letmeseethecolts proves too strong for Animato in the final furlong while the closers arrive too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sweet Kiss Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the Easterby mare produces her best form after two disappointing runs this season.
scenarios.body: Her three wins under Dickson last year suggest she has untapped ability at this trip and conditions. The moderate early pace allows her to deliver a withering late charge that catches the leaders napping.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Animato Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the veteran finds his old stamina and the field fails to mount serious challenges.
scenarios.body: Despite his recent hurdling campaign, his five flat wins suggest he retains class when fresh. The lack of early pace pressure allows him to control the race from pillar to post.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Animato gets an uncontested lead as multiple hold-up horses will converge late and could catch him napping
Monitor Letmeseethecolts early positioning as she needs to be prominent to have any chance given recent struggles
Observe Sweet Kiss's early movement under Dickson as any signs of her old enthusiasm could signal a return to form
Check Division Day's fitness levels after four months off as stamina could be compromised despite suitable race shape
Note Muhib's finishing kick given his 14lb weight advantage through the apprentice claim

races.name: Support Weston Park Cancer Charity Today Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: My Mate Roger
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent form who should benefit if the pace-setters engage early, though 25 days off the track
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in all three starts and sets useful standard on his close call at Windsor latest
runners_data.spotlight: 75,000euros breeze-up 2yo; finished runner-up in his three starts since December including a near-miss when upped to 1m2f at Windsor (good to firm) last month; sets useful standard on that form and his RPRs have been progressive so far; strong contender.

runners_data.name: Hawksworth
runners_data.note: Debutant from struggling Quinn stable with excellent breeding but trainer form of 0/11 in last 14 days raises concerns
runners_data.comment: 23,000euros yearling; already been gelded and this looks a tough starting point
runners_data.spotlight: 23,000euros yearling; first foal; dam placed 7f-8.6f 2yo (RPR 79), out of unraced sister to Group-placed 1m4f winner Sayida, half-sister to Derby winner Masar; already been gelded and this looks a tough starting point.

runners_data.name: Ingemar
runners_data.note: Newcomer from stronger Meehan yard with Group-class pedigree, though trainer also quiet recently at 0/5
runners_data.comment: 42,000euros yearling; has good target to aim at on debut and market should guide
runners_data.spotlight: 42,000euros yearling; ninth foal; gelded half-brother to 1m Group 3 winner Indian Blessing and two useful French midde-distance winners; dam useful 1m2f/1m4f winner; has good target to aim at on debut and market should guide.

runners_data.name: Le Morbihan
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who showed decent form last time and will look to dictate from the front
runners_data.comment: Showed promise on Beverley debut and he should benefit from that experience
runners_data.spotlight: 65,000euros yearling; dam unraced sister to 7f/8.6f 2yo winner Pomelo, half-sister to Group 1 scorers Bluestocking (1m2f/1m4f including Arc) and Qirat (1m Sussex Stakes); 22-1 at Beverley (1m2f, good) in April but he ran well for a long way and was beaten only about 4l in fourth of eight; this is a tougher assignment but that was an encouraging start and he should benefit from the experience.

runners_data.name: Harmonics
runners_data.note: Hold-up type in good form having won last time out on all-weather, though this turf debut poses questions
runners_data.comment: Won at Southwell last month and he's open to more progress upped in trip; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Made a low-key start at Southwell (1m, AW) in April but he left that form well behind when beating 11 rivals on his return visit (7-2) two weeks ago; this is tougher under a penalty but he has a useful pedigree and is open to more progress on this step up in trip; respected.

runners_data.name: I Got Rhythm
runners_data.note: Rear-division runner who was well beaten on debut and likely needs this experience
runners_data.comment: 80-1 and was always in rear throughout on his Newmarket debut (1m, good) last month
runners_data.spotlight: 80-1 and was always in rear throughout on his Newmarket debut (1m, good) last month; was beaten around 16l in that race and he's probably a longer-term prospect.

runners_data.name: West Sleekburn Lad
runners_data.note: Struggling hold-up horse returning from 230-day layoff with poor debut form
runners_data.comment: 66-1 and he failed to beat a rival on Catterick debut in October; best watched on return
runners_data.spotlight: Missed the break and was always behind when last of ten on his Catterick debut (7f, good; 66-1) in October; best watched on return.

runners_data.name: Cliff Danger
runners_data.note: Front-running gelding who shaped better last time after wind operation, should press for early lead
runners_data.comment: Showed promise over 1m2f at Nottingham and has each-way claims if he can build on that
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't show a great deal on Wetherby debut (1m) in April but, after a gelding operation, he shaped with promise when fourth at Nottingham (1m2f, good to soft) last month; has each-way claims if he can take another step forward and he's in the mix.

runners_data.name: Annahita
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with modest form but gets significant weight allowance, though 38 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Down the field in both runs and handicaps look the way forward after this
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form when down the field at Kempton (1m, AW) in October and she was beaten 16l on her Lingfield reappearance (11-2) last month; still early days but she has a lot to find here and handicaps will be more suitable.

races.paceDynamic: Cliff Danger and Le Morbihan will contest the early lead, with both showing front-running tendencies and likely to set an honest gallop over this 1m2f trip. The pace should be genuine rather than crawling given these two confirmed pace-setters, creating a scenario where the field gets strung out. With most of the field consisting of hold-up horses (My Mate Roger, Harmonics, I Got Rhythm, West Sleekburn Lad, Annahita), they'll need the leaders to soften each other up. This race shape clearly favours the prominent/midfield runners who can track the pace without getting embroiled in the early battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Softens Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Cliff Danger and Le Morbihan engage in a sustained pace battle from the outset.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners will compromise each other's finishing kicks, allowing the hold-up horses to close strongly in the final two furlongs. My Mate Roger and Harmonics are best positioned to capitalize with their proven ability to finish from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Single Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters gains an uncontested lead while the other settles behind.
scenarios.body: The lone leader will dictate terms and prove difficult to peg back, particularly if Le Morbihan can utilize his front-running style without pressure. The hold-up brigade will struggle to make up the ground on good to firm going.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Newcomers Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the lightly-raced Hawksworth or Ingemar possess significantly more ability than their debuts suggest.
scenarios.body: One of the newcomers will benefit from tracking the early pace battle and emerge late with superior class. Their breeding suggests middle-distance potential that could unlock at this 1m2f trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Early Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If both pace-setters are cautious early and the gallop becomes moderate.
scenarios.body: A tactical affair would suit horses that can quicken from prominent positions rather than pure hold-up types. The race would become a sprint finish where natural speed matters more than stamina.

watchPoints.text: Le Morbihan and Cliff Danger could engage in a pace duel that sets up the race perfectly for the closers
Watch if either newcomer Hawksworth or Ingemar travels strongly early, suggesting they possess more ability than expected
Monitor how quickly My Mate Roger gets into contention given his 25-day break and hold-up style
If the early pace is moderate rather than honest, it could turn into a sprint finish favoring different profiles
Harmonics making turf debut after all-weather win needs to handle the surface change successfully

races.name: Hits Radio Proudly Supports WPCC Novice Stakes Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Master Of Delphi
runners_data.note: Expensive yearling making debut for moderate stable with poor 14-day record, unknown pace style but breeding suggests he could show early speed.
runners_data.comment: 150,000euros breeze-up 2yo; has useful standard to aim at on debut and market should guide
runners_data.spotlight: $100,000 yearling, 150,000euros breeze-up 2yo; seventh foal; gelded half-brother to winners Desert Peace (7f-1m2f AW/dirt including 2yo; RPR 98), Cantata (6.5f 2yo/8.5f dirt) and Mission Beach (5f-6.5f turf/dirt including 2yo); dam US 4.5f dirt 2yo winner (including stakes); this looks a tough starting point but interesting to see how he figures in market.

runners_data.name: Upper East
runners_data.note: Hannon debutant from strong stable with 300,000gns price tag, completely unknown quantity but trainer excels with expensive newcomers first time out.
runners_data.comment: 300,000gns yearling; has useful target to aim at on debut but he needs checking in market
runners_data.spotlight: 300,000gns yearling; second foal; dam 5.7f/6f winner (RPR 89), half-sister to smart 1m-1m6f winner Micro Manage and Listed winners Magnanimous (1m), Thornbrook (1m) and Seisai (7.4f 2yo), out of close relative of 1m4f Group 1 winner Mont Ormel; has useful target to aim on debut but he needs watching in market.

runners_data.name: Impierious
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 50 days break, needs pace to aim at and the likely tactical nature of this small field may not suit his running style.
runners_data.comment: Promising third in the Wood Ditton and he should know more this time; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Closely related to 1m-1m4f winner Mashhoor (including Group 3; RPR 115) and he's a half-brother to seven winners; beaten 8l when third in the Wood Ditton at Newmarket (1m, good) in April but he looked inexperienced and that was a promising effort behind an impressive winner; should know more this time and he's a likely improver on his second start.

runners_data.name: Forever Endless
runners_data.note: Remote fifth on debut at 80-1, hold-up horse who needs significant pace improvement and a strong gallop to be competitive here.
runners_data.comment: 80-1 and he finished a remote fifth of six on Nottingham debut (8.3f, good) last month
runners_data.spotlight: 80-1 and he finished a remote fifth of six on Nottingham debut (8.3f, good) last month; opposable.

runners_data.name: Ruler Of Time
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with clear pace advantage, 126 days since last run but Appleby runners often go well fresh, sets the standard on ratings.
runners_data.spotlight: RPR of 87 when runner-up in three of his four starts including a close second in a big-field handicap at Meydan (1m, good) in January; just about sets the standard on his return and he should have more to offer at this trip; key player.

runners_data.name: Seet
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who impressed on debut before disappointing second start, Gosden stable in good form and the step up to a mile should help.
runners_data.comment: Well-bred filly who won in good style at Wolverhampton last month; respected under penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to five winners including Kalpana (8.6f-1m4f including Group 1; RPR 123); shaped with promise on Newbury debut (7f, good) in April and she found plenty of progress when scoring in good style on the step up to 8.6f at Wolverhampton (100-30) last month; has a penalty back on turf but she looks a smart prospect and is strongly respected.

runners_data.name: Electric Dreams
runners_data.note: Non-runner, well-held in previous starts and wouldn't have threatened the main contenders based on current form levels.
runners_data.comment: Well held in both runs this spring and this looks a tough assignment
runners_data.spotlight: 475,000gns yearling; didn't live up to market expectations on Kempton debut (1m, AW) in April and was well held again at Newbury (1m2f, good) last month; still early days but this looks a tough assignment and handicaps will be more suitable.

races.paceDynamic: Ruler Of Time is the only confirmed front runner and will likely lead from the start, setting a sustainable pace without pressure from other prominent racers. With Master Of Delphi and Upper East as unknown quantities but potentially having pace, there's a slim chance of early pressure, but more likely Ruler Of Time gets an easy lead with the field bunched behind. The majority of runners (Impierious, Forever Endless, Seet, Electric Dreams) are hold-up types who will need the pace to develop. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those who can track the leader closely, as the lack of genuine pace pressure will make it difficult for hold-up horses to close from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Ruler Of Time gets an uncontested lead with no early pace pressure from the newcomers.
scenarios.body: The Appleby runner controls the tempo throughout and has enough in reserve to kick clear in the final furlong, making it very difficult for the hold-up horses to close the gap. His RPR 98 and previous course-and-distance experience gives him a clear edge when dictating terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Newcomer Shows Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Master Of Delphi or Upper East shows early pace to press or challenge Ruler Of Time.
scenarios.body: The injection of pace pressure creates a faster gallop that sets up the race for the hold-up horses, with Seet and Impierious getting the strong tempo they need. The early pace battle compromises the front runners in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Godolphin Experience Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a tactical affair with slow fractions throughout.
scenarios.body: Ruler Of Time's superior racecourse experience and higher RPR rating allows him to quicken best from the steady pace, but Seet's Gosden training and breeding gives her the class edge in a sprint finish. The lack of pace favours those with natural acceleration.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If unexpected pace materializes from multiple sources creating a strong gallop.
scenarios.body: Impierious and Seet get the searching test they need, with the honest pace allowing them to unleash their finishing kicks from off the tempo. The pace collapse in the final two furlongs plays directly into their patient tactics.

watchPoints.text: If Master Of Delphi or Upper East show any early pace in the market or paddock, as this could completely change the race dynamics and create the gallop the hold-up horses need.
Watch Ruler Of Time's fitness after 126 days off, as any lack of sharpness could allow the field to close on him despite the tactical advantage.
Monitor Seet's settling early on, as she needs to drop out and get cover to maximize her finishing kick from this likely slow pace scenario.
Check the ground conditions remain good to firm as advertised, since any ease in the going could particularly disadvantage the newcomers.
Observe how aggressively Zac Lloyd rides Ruler Of Time early, as setting too slow a pace could invite pressure from unexpected sources.

races.name: Rotabroach Proudly Supports WPCC Handicap

runners_data.name: King's Cavalry
runners_data.note: Prominent runner facing traffic danger in congested battle, but class edge from recent Leicester win gives him best chance of prominent group
runners_data.comment: Easy odds-on win at Leicester and he's an interesting contender on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Kingman colt who made it third-time lucky when landing the odds in good style at Leicester (7f, good to firm) last month; looks on a workable mark now switched to a handicap and this related colt should have more to offer; interesting contender.

runners_data.name: Toastmaster
runners_data.note: Another prominent runner likely to get caught in traffic, but consistent form suggests he can handle the scrap better than most
runners_data.comment: 0-8 but was a close third in big-field handicap at York on recent stable debut; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 but he was consistent for the Crisfords and made a good start for new yard when close third in big-field handicap at York (7f, good) last month; ties in closely with French Affair on that form and he's in the mix.

runners_data.name: Rogue Messiah
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts him in the danger zone, stepping up in trip after 6f success but breeding suggests he'll handle 7f
runners_data.comment: Record of 2-4 for Jack Jones and he's open to more progress upped to 7f for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed gelding who won two of his four starts for Jack Jones, including on handicap debut at Lingfield (6f, AW) in April; up 5lb but he's bred to stay this extra furlong and is open to more progress on his first run for James Owen; respected.

runners_data.name: Blakefell
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to this pace shape, fresh from wind surgery success but this is much stronger company
runners_data.comment: Won after wind surgery at Musselburgh but this is tougher on handicap debut; needs more
runners_data.spotlight: Returned after wind surgery with a Musselburgh maiden win (7f, good) two weeks ago, but he didn't need to improve to take that prize; still unexposed but this is a deeper race on handicap debut and others are preferred.

runners_data.name: King's Trust
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with Gosden training but stalls antics last time are concerning, headgear applied suggests issues
runners_data.comment: Southwell winner but he's blotted his copybook since; needs to raise his game back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Beat one who is now on a mark of 95 off level weights at Southwell last October (7f); blotted his copybook by playing up before breaking out of the stalls on intended seasonal/handicap debut in 1m contest at Ascot last month; looked more relaxed at Kempton last week but he never got involved from a wide draw; still early days but he needs to raise his game back on turf.

runners_data.name: French Affair
runners_data.note: Prominent style faces traffic problems, one win from eleven starts suggests he lacks killer instinct in these scraps
runners_data.comment: Record of 1-11 but he went close in a 20-runner handicap at York last time; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win from 11 starts but he hit a personal best when going close in a 20-runner handicap at York (7f, good) last month; the first three pulled clear in that race and he's strongly respected off only 1lb higher.

runners_data.name: Valpovo
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with 223 days off creating huge unknown factor, but solo French win suggests ability if fit
runners_data.comment: Won in France on the second of three 2yo runs; needs close look on handicap/stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Had three runs in France as a 2yo and he won at La Teste De Buch (9.5f, heavy) on his second start; changed hands for 40,000gns in October; returns after 223 days off but he has a striking pedigree and needs watching in market on handicap/stable debut.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but poor recent form trend and trainer's 0/10 record are major concerns
runners_data.comment: Three wins at 7f but he's been well held in last three runs and is exposed after 12 starts
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins have come over 7f and latest was at Southwell in March; only 2lb higher than for that win but he's finished down the field in last three runs and he's the most exposed runner in this line-up; passed over.

runners_data.name: Thunder Call
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with perfect race shape, Haggas/Marquand combination and breeding suggest more to come
runners_data.comment: Easy win in Kempton maiden (6f) last month and he's a big player again on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Well-bred colt who is closely related to 7f 2yo/1m Group 3 winner Skardu (RPR 114); left his initial form well behind when runner-up here (6f, heavy) in November and he found more improvement with an emphatic win on his Kempton reappearance (6f, AW) last month; now goes back up in trip but he looks a useful prospect and is a big player for in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Sanaam
runners_data.note: Solo leader with uncontested lead advantage, but disappointing handicap debut at Wetherby raises questions about competitive desire
runners_data.comment: Disappointing on handicap debut at Wetherby and his standout form was on sole AW start
runners_data.spotlight: Forged clear in a Southwell maiden (7f, Tapeta) towards the end of last year but he was disappointing on handicap debut at Wetherby (7f, good to firm; 4-1) in April; has bit to prove again after that 8l defeat and his standout form was on his sole AW run.

runners_data.name: Night Patrol
runners_data.note: Prominent runner adding to congestion problems, shock 125-1 winner suggests limited ability despite Camacho switch
runners_data.comment: 125-1 winner at Newbury last September but he's not gone on from that in two runs since
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Newbury novice (7f, good to soft) for Richard Hannon last September but that was a shock at 125-1 and he's not gone on from that in two handicaps since; still lightly raced but he was out the back on recent stable debut at Beverley (first run since gelded) and others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Peel Park
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with good going record but 11-length Ascot defeat shows he's struggling at current level
runners_data.comment: No joy in four handicaps and he needs a transformation back in trip; blinkers added
runners_data.spotlight: Won Yarmouth maiden (6f, good to firm) last July but he's found things tough in four handicaps since; dropped another 3lb but he was beaten 11l at Ascot last month and he needs a transformation back in trip; blinkers added.

races.paceDynamic: Sanaam is the only confirmed front runner and will set a sustainable pace without pressure early. Five horses (King's Cavalry, Toastmaster, Rogue Messiah, King's Trust, French Affair) all want prominent positions, creating dangerous congestion and traffic problems turning for home. The solo leader advantage combined with hold-up horses getting a perfect setup behind the prominently-placed traffic jam strongly favours front runners and closers. This pace shape clearly benefits lead and hold-up runners over the congested prominent brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Sanaam gets soft sectionals and the prominent pack bunches up
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader kicks clear while prominent runners get in each other's way 2f out. Hold-up horses pick off the faltering prominent group but can't catch the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates a messy pace and strong gallop late
scenarios.body: The five prominent runners compromise each other's chances allowing patient hold-up horses perfect racing room. Late closers sweep past the tiring prominently-raced field in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Royale
scenarios.trigger: If King's Cavalry or Toastmaster break clear from the prominent pack early
scenarios.body: One of the classier prominent runners escapes the traffic and sustains their effort better than rivals. The winner emerges from a fierce battle between the well-positioned horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The tactical race becomes a pure speed test favouring fresher horses with less exposure. An outsider with hidden ability capitalizes on the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Sanaam must be watched for early tempo - if he goes too fast early the hold-up horses become unbeatable
King's Trust stalls behaviour after breaking out last time - any pre-race antics could ruin his chances
The prominent quintet (King's Cavalry, Toastmaster, Rogue Messiah, King's Trust, French Affair) for traffic problems turning in
Valpovo for fitness after 223 days off - any market move would be highly significant
Thunder Call for Marquand's positioning tactics - his ride could determine if the hold-up scenario unfolds

races.name: Apus Life Sciences Handicap

runners_data.name: City Of Kings
runners_data.note: Sole front runner returning from 1144 days off, but has class advantage and won't face early pressure
runners_data.comment: Very lightly raced 6yo but he has plenty to prove after a mammoth absence; new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Won Ascot maiden (7f, good) for Charlie Appleby in 2022 but he has been absent, gelded and sold for 140,000AED since well held in conditions event at Newmarket the following spring; this is only his fourth run but he returns after a 1,144 days off and has plenty to prove for another new yard.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner who prefers to track the pace, excellent recent form at York
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D winner who reappeared with a good fourth at Newmarket last month; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won twice over C&D last summer and he defied this mark when beating 15 rivals at York last September; reappeared with a creditable fourth at Newmarket last month and he's a big player if he can build on that.

runners_data.name: Tilted Kilt
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with headgear change (tongue-tie), suits the likely tactical nature
runners_data.comment: Reappeared with a win at Southwell (1m) but he was down the field at Ascot last month
runners_data.spotlight: Belatedly doubled his tally when beating five rivals on his Southwell reappearance (1m) in April; still looks feasibly treated but he's hard to predict and was never involved when a well-held seventh at Ascot last month.

runners_data.name: Talis Evolvere
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but poor turf record (1-20) makes him vulnerable
runners_data.comment: Five-time AW winner but he's 1-20 on turf and has been well held in his last three runs
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time AW winner but he's 1-20 on turf and has been well held over this trip in last two runs; down the list.

runners_data.name: Cavolo Nero
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with blinkers, good course form and benefits from steady early pace
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice as a 3yo and latest was at Goodwood (1m, good); didn't shine at Haydock (10.4f) when last seen in April but that was behind a subsequent winner and he was runner-up at Kempton (1m, AW) in March; has claims if he can recapture that form and he's not ruled out back in trip; new headgear.

runners_data.name: It'sneverjustone
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but 48 days since last run and 3lb higher than last win
runners_data.comment: Two solid efforts this season and he looks worth another try at this trip; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: All of his 14 runs have been on good or slower and he won back-to-back handicaps at Ffos Las (7.3f) and Galway (7f) last summer; still 3lb higher than for last success but he's finished a creditable fourth in both runs this season and he looks worth another try at this trip; dangerous.

runners_data.name: Intrusively
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with visor, only maiden winner but improving form recently
runners_data.comment: Back to form with eye-catching fourth at Nottingham last month; interesting contender
runners_data.spotlight: His sole win was in a maiden in August 2024 but he turned things around with a close fourth at Nottingham (8.3f, good) last month; didn't get the best of runs in that race and has claims if he can back that up.

runners_data.name: Sailthisshipalone
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form, won on stable debut and ran well last time
runners_data.comment: Won at Pontefract on his penultimate run and was a good fourth there latest; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Recorded his third win when scoring on stable debut at Pontefract (1m, good to soft) in April and he ran to a similar level when a creditable fourth on his return visit three weeks later; should go well again and he seems fairly versatile ground-wise; cheekpieces reapplied.

runners_data.name: Mr Mistoffelees
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but poor recent form (0-12 on turf) despite dangerous mark
runners_data.comment: Both of his wins have been on AW and he's been well held in three runs this season
runners_data.spotlight: On dangerous mark but he's finished down the field in three runs this term and is now 0-12 in Flat turf events; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Cadarn
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who's been disappointing since winning two at Redcar last spring
runners_data.comment: Two wins at Redcar last spring but he's been disappointing since; needs a major revival
runners_data.spotlight: Won two in a row at Redcar (1m, good to firm) last spring for George Boughey; now 2lb lower than for his last success but he's been disappointing since including for new yard this spring; this is a big drop back in grade but he reared at the start at York last time and others are more convincing.

runners_data.name: Rumba Numba
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly returning from 311 days off but unexposed on turf
runners_data.comment: Unexposed filly who still has potential and needs a close look on her comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo who won a Wolverhampton maiden (8.6f, AW) last May and she didn't get much luck when fourth on handicap debut at Glorious Goodwood (1m, good) last summer; now returns after 311 days off but she still has potential and is an interesting contender off the same mark as last time.

runners_data.name: Miletus
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for new trainer but only one win from 14 career starts
runners_data.comment: Some creditable efforts for new yard this season and he has claims back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win from 14 starts came in a soft-ground novice at Windsor (1m) in May 2024 when trained by Charlie Hills; four runs for new yard this year and he's finished runner-up twice, including over 7f here (good to soft) on his penultimate run; has possibilities back up in trip and it would be a positive if the forecast rain arrives; hood worn last time is removed.

runners_data.name: Bowood
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with apprentice jockey, 119 days since last run and AW specialist
runners_data.comment: All of his wins have been in lower grades and this is competitive on return; down the list
runners_data.spotlight: Two clearcut wins at Newcastle (1m, AW) last autumn but he wasn't at his best on Tapeta during the winter; has scored over C&D in the past but he's never won a Class 4 and this is competitive on his return; others preferred.

races.paceDynamic: City Of Kings is the sole confirmed front runner and will likely set a steady pace without pressure from fellow prominent runners Canvas, Talis Evolvere, and It'sneverjustone who prefer to track rather than lead. This creates a tactical race where the pace will build gradually rather than be cutthroat early. The large field of 13 runners includes many hold-up horses like Tilted Kilt, Cavolo Nero, Intrusively, and Mr Mistoffelees who will be relying on the race developing into a sprint finish. This pace scenario clearly favours the hold-up horses and late closers who can capitalise on a steady early gallop and strong finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If City Of Kings sets a modest pace without early pressure from the prominent runners
scenarios.body: The steady early tempo allows the large contingent of hold-up horses to get into perfect position before unleashing their finishing kicks. Horses like Tilted Kilt, Cavolo Nero, and Rumba Numba benefit from the tactical nature and sprint home past tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Canvas or Talis Evolvere apply more pressure to City Of Kings than expected
scenarios.body: The increased pace puts pressure on the hold-up horses to make their moves earlier while suiting those positioned prominently. Canvas particularly benefits as he's proven over course and distance with winning form here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If City Of Kings gets an uncontested lead and the field allows him too much rope
scenarios.body: His class advantage from his Ascot maiden win for Charlie Appleby shows through as he maintains his advantage to the line. The lack of early pressure allows him to dictate terms despite his long absence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners fail to apply any pressure and the pace becomes pedestrian
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the 3f pole which suits horses with tactical pace like Miletus and those who can quicken sharply. The very slow tempo catches out some hold-up horses who get too far back.

watchPoints.text: City Of Kings could steal this if given too easy a lead given his superior class background despite the long layoff
Canvas is the most reliable option given his course and distance winning record and recent York form
Tilted Kilt's tongue-tie headgear change could spark improvement in what should be an ideal tactical scenario
The large field of hold-up horses could get in each other's way if the pace is too steady
Rumba Numba represents the Varian stable returning from a break and showed promise at Goodwood

races.name: Join Us To Walk As One Handicap

runners_data.name: Mythical Phoenix
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with recent slow starts, 174 days off presents major fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Last solid run came when fourth in this last year; mark fine if 174-day break has helped
runners_data.spotlight: A solid run when fourth in this race (good) last year but he struggled subsequently, with slow starts also becoming a feature; handicapped to be competitive if a 174-day break has freshened him up.

runners_data.name: Photosynthesis
runners_data.note: Prominent racer building on Newbury fourth, lively in spring betting suggests connections confident
runners_data.comment: Solid fourth (6f, good) last time and he's respected from the same mark
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark for this stable at Newmarket in September; lively in the betting for both starts this spring and he built on a midfield finish at Newbury when fourth of ten at Ascot (again 6f, good) four weeks ago; respected from the same mark.

runners_data.name: Lord Bertie
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with poor course record on good ground, 7lb claimer adds uncertainty
runners_data.comment: C&D winner but finished last behind Novello Lad three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Eight visits to Doncaster yielded one soft-ground win over this trip in October; made an encouraging return when sixth of 19 in March but didn't back that up when last behind Novello Lad (again C&D, good to soft) three weeks ago; he's not the most uncomplicated but mark is fine if he can bounce back.

runners_data.name: Novello Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with recent C&D win but 8lb rise makes task much harder from back of field
runners_data.comment: Second C&D win last time; 8lb rise sets a task but he can never be discounted here
runners_data.spotlight: Track regular who added a second C&D win to his record on good to soft three weeks ago; handicapper handed him an 8lb rise but that looked a career best and he can never be discounted at this venue.

runners_data.name: Papa Cocktail
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong C&D record (3-1-2), racing off same mark as recent second
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed sprinter who wins in his turn these days but his C&D record reads 312; that latest visit was just one month ago and he competes from the same mark as when far from disgraced in midfield at York a fortnight ago; each-way contender.

runners_data.name: Bright
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won here in 2024 on good to firm, last turf success was that Doncaster victory
runners_data.spotlight: Both visits here came in the summer of 2024 and yielded a third followed by a win, both at 6f on good to firm; that was his last success on turf but he scored on AW three starts back and last month's return to grass from the widest stall at Chester can be ignored; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Kats Bob
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who tends to lead, excellent record for Ruth Carr but 14th last time disappointing
runners_data.comment: Tends to lead; now 2lb below last winning mark; case to be made but well held latest
runners_data.spotlight: Tends to lead; hit the ground running by winning his first four starts for Ruth Carr last year; plenty of good efforts followed including when he beat 18 others to score at York (6f, good to firm) in June; now 2lb below that last winning mark so a handicapping case to be made, but he did not sustain his effort when finishing well held at York a fortnight ago.

runners_data.name: Smart Vision
runners_data.note: Prominent/lead runner with two course wins, only confirmed pace-setter but poor recent form
runners_data.spotlight: Versatile regards ground; six wins include two here (7f/5f) and he was second in this race last year; yet to get going this term but there was the faintest hint he might be on the way back at Chester (5f) last time and maybe the return to this trip can help; mark fine.

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who lost form badly, beaten only one home in both starts for O'Meara
runners_data.comment: Has lost his way and best watched for now unless the market suggests otherwise
runners_data.spotlight: Group 3 win and Group 1 third in France as a 2yo but lost his form in 2025 and beat only one home in both starts for this yard last month; best watched unless the market suggests otherwise.

runners_data.name: Alondra
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner improving for Scott Dixon, 7 days between runs could be too quick
runners_data.comment: Dual 5f AW winner in February; 6f okay and has form on turf; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) in February on just her second start for this yard and defied a penalty over that C&D four days later; creditable effort when sharing third over this trip at Southwell (AW) in April and maybe the cheekpieces backfired when fifth at Wolverhampton one week ago; that equipment is now removed and she has form on turf, so she's not ruled out.

runners_data.name: American Style
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who goes well fresh, close third on comeback suggests fitness ready
runners_data.comment: Heavy defeat latest but this is a drop back in grade so he's not completely dismissed
runners_data.spotlight: Goes well fresh and he scored on his seasonal/handicap debut last April; again ran well when close third off this mark on his comeback (also Ripon, 6f) this term; he didn't back it up when suffering a heavy defeat at York last time, albeit from a poor draw, but this represents a drop back in grade so he's not dismissed.

runners_data.name: Media Darling
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 237-day break, debut winner last year but huge layoff concern
runners_data.spotlight: Made her debut only ten months ago and she bagged an Ayr maiden (6f, good to firm) in August on second start; couldn't defy a penalty on AW next time, while a swing at a Listed race proved beyond her when last seen; look for market interest on this handicap/seasonal debut.

runners_data.name: Tough Enough
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with hood removed last time, second at Southwell suggests returning to form
runners_data.spotlight: Dual turf winner who last won in August 2023; had reduced mark and regular hood removed when back to some form for second of six at Southwell (6f, AW; Alondra third) in April; could be rediscovering his level and he's not dismissed from the same mark.

runners_data.name: Kirkdale
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins (6f, AW) in April; totally unexposed at 6f on turf; key contender
runners_data.spotlight: Soft-ground 7f winner as a juvenile who hit form with back-to-back wins at Wolverhampton and Southwell (again 6f, AW) in April; pulled out twice from intended engagements last month but he's totally unexposed at 6f on turf and will be a key contender in the hat-trick bid if in the same mood.

runners_data.name: Betties Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner completing four-timer last month, still improving and low weight helps
runners_data.comment: Rampant mare who completed a four-timer latest, going 4-4 for yard; impossible to ignore
runners_data.spotlight: Rampant mare who completed a four-timer when coming back from a break to score at Catterick (6f, good) last month; that made it 4-4 for this yard and she's still competitively weighted on form for her previous stable; impossible to ignore.

races.paceDynamic: Smart Vision is the sole confirmed front runner with Kats Bob (who tends to lead) and American Style likely to press early. This creates a manageable pace rather than a sprint burn-up, with the prominent runners getting an honest tempo without destructive pressure. The large field of 15 means hold-up horses will need clear runs and luck in running over the minimum trip. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those able to track the pace, as they avoid traffic problems while benefiting from a sustainable gallop that won't leave them empty late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Smart Vision and Kats Bob set a steady honest pace without getting into a speed duel early
scenarios.body: The pace-tracking horses get perfect positioning while hold-up runners struggle for room in the large field. Photosynthesis and American Style are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong and the prominent runners tie up in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Late runners with clear passages benefit from the honest gallop sapping the leaders' reserves. Novello Lad's recent C&D win and Papa Cocktail's course form become decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Smart Vision Wire Job
scenarios.trigger: If Smart Vision gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The front runner capitalizes on soft fractions to build an unassailable advantage. Hold-up horses left with too much to do despite the honest pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Smart Vision and Kats Bob go too fast early and completely tie up
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole favouring horses with tactical speed. Those held up closest become best placed for the dash.

watchPoints.text: Smart Vision could get too easy a lead if Kats Bob doesn't engage early, creating unassailable advantage
Media Darling faces fitness test after 237 days off, despite connections booking Tom Marquand
Lord Bertie struggles on good ground at Doncaster with poor course record
Novello Lad carries 8lb rise for recent C&D win, significant penalty for hold-up horse in large field
American Style's fresh record suggests he could improve sharply on Ripon comeback third

runners_data.spotlight: Reached the frame in his three 2yo runs (7f), but he returned after a gelding operation with a laboured efforts on handicap debut at Haydock (1m, good) last month; has bit to prove after that and he needs improvement at this new trip.

runners_data.name: Faeberon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with big improvement after gelding operation, third at Thirsk suggests upward trajectory

runners_data.spotlight: Kicked off his handicap career with a close second over C&D (good to firm) in April but he failed to back that up when ninth of 14 at Newbury last month; still unexposed but he needs to resume his progress back at this track.

runners_data.name: Attention Seeker

runners_data.comment: Regressive nine-race maiden who was well held over 1m2f at Beverley latest; passed over

races.paceDynamic: Battosai is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate proceedings uncontested from the off. Five horses (Turtle Reef, Aerial Silk, Faeberon, Filly Eilish, Domination, Attention Seeker) all want prominent positions behind him, creating significant congestion and traffic issues turning for home. The hold-up pair Dryburgh and Madjid (both flagged as fading in the finish) plus Howsham will be coming from the rear down the long Doncaster straight. This race shape strongly favours the lone leader Battosai and any hold-up horses who can avoid the mid-race scramble and time their challenge perfectly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Battosai gets an easy lead and the prominent pack neutralize each other in traffic
scenarios.body: The leader gets first run turning in while the prominent brigade are still sorting themselves out, giving him the decisive advantage. Dryburgh has the class to pick up pieces from the rear but may not have enough time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Times It
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack go hard early trying to get position behind Battosai
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will set up perfectly for the closers, with Dryburgh's recent form improvement and Tom Marquand's tactical nous crucial. Madjid could also benefit if overcoming his finishing concerns.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent pack (likely Faeberon or Domination) gets first run from the traffic
scenarios.body: Either Faeberon builds on his Thirsk third or Domination rediscovers his Ripon winning form, getting the jump on rivals still stuck behind horses. The leader may tire late having done the donkey work.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Battosai goes too slow early and the prominent pack stays bunched throughout
scenarios.body: A messy sprint finish develops where any of the prominent runners could prevail, with Filly Eilish's light weight potentially decisive. Positioning and racing room become lottery elements.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems 2f out when 5-6 prominent runners all want the same racing room behind Battosai
Monitor Battosai's early fractions - if too slow he invites pressure, if too fast he may not last home
Watch Dryburgh's position turning in - needs to be within striking distance to use his superior finishing kick
Check how quickly the prominent pack settle - early scrimmaging will play into the closers' hands
Observe Faeberon's jumping from the stalls - needs to secure good early position to avoid the squeeze
